A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiCache and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 adds Appendices A–H, which were included in the comparison. No material reading gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation comparisons, feature analyses and component ablations, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sparse-attention compatibility results, cache-order ablations and further qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces and evaluates a decay-weighted higher-order DCTA variant using additional historical caches. The main online-probe procedure and two-cache first-order estimator remain unchanged, and first order remains the selected default.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-video generation using collected prompts and text-to-image generation using LAION-5B captions. Additional examples and the separate 500-caption ablation retain this coverage. WAN 2.1 14B adds a model configuration, not a distinct task or dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership, including image-only ToCa. New Table 3 evaluates Sparse VideoGen alone against Sparse VideoGen plus DiCache; v1 cited Sparse VideoGen but did not report this comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation configurations: HunyuanVideo with sparse attention at 720×1280 and 129 frames on an H200 140GB GPU, a separate 500-caption Flux cache-order experiment, and WAN 2.1 14B qualitative tests. The original 300-prompt video and 1K-caption image protocols remain unchanged; these are additional evaluations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained probe-depth, threshold and DCTA ablations, v2 tests compatibility with sparse attention in Table 3/Figure 14, cache orders 0, 1, 2 and 4 in Table 4, and sensitivity to seeds for fixed prompts in Figure 13. These add substantive composability, design-choice and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 3(d) adds variability bands to the previously unbanded Spearman-correlation curves. Appendix C/Figure 13 explicitly reports seeds 0, 1 and 2 for qualitative comparisons. No increase in repeated runs or new confidence intervals for the main benchmark tables is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New Table 3 reports speedups relative to vanilla of 1.67× for SVG and 3.08× for SVG plus DiCache, with LPIPS worsening from 0.1760 to 0.2051. New Table 4 reports Flux LPIPS of 0.2930, 0.2691, 0.2686 and 0.2710 for cache orders 0, 1, 2 and 4. Revised Figure 3 curves and additional qualitative results further expand the evidence; these are not same-setting improvements over v1's benchmarks.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a formal higher-order residual approximation, a decay factor and corresponding probe-based coefficient expressions in Equations 13–16. The original mathematical development in Equations 1–11 is retained; no new theorem or error-bound proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: shallow-layer probes determine cache timing and guide trajectory alignment, improving inference efficiency and fidelity across WAN, HunyuanVideo and Flux. The stronger emphasis on sample-specific adaptation clarifies an idea already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the small benefits of higher cache orders against their memory burden, supporting the first-order choice. Section 4.4 discusses compatibility with sparse attention, and the new limitations section explicitly identifies residual probing overhead and reducing it as future work.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies video resolutions and absolute sampling budgets of 50 steps for both video models and 30 for Flux. v2 also supplies figure prompts, H200 configurations and the new ablation's decay factor of 0.5. A project-page link is added while the existing repository link is retained; actual online availability was not assessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Peebles and Xie's diffusion-transformer work and Wu et al.'s Qwen-image report. The central positioning against caching methods dependent on offline priors or handcrafted rules remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized abstract, introduction and method rewrites emphasize sample-specific indicators and streamline explanations. Related-work subsections become paragraph headings, limitations and appendix sections are added, and Tong Wu/Stanford are removed from the author block. The main narrative remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 7–14 and Tables 3–5, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Existing displays are also revised: Figure 1 replaces video examples, Figure 3 changes plotting and labeling, Figure 5 moves, Figure 6 gains prompt annotations, and Tables 1–2 receive formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit sampling configurations and prompts, and strengthens support for the retained design through compatibility and cache-order tests. The main benchmark findings remain unchanged. The gains are limited by qualitative seed checks and optimistic interpretation of Table 3, whose additional speed comes with worse fidelity metrics.
